01 / STUDY RECORD

What was run

The final scope contains the first five papers in the prior ICLR2026 source order. Every selected version was reviewed independently under every condition.

OBSERVATION 01

No OA shifts

Three papers received only 3 — Reject; two received only 1 — Strong Reject. This holds across all selected versions and all thirteen conditions.

OBSERVATION 02

Different explanations

All 234 complete results have different text. Stable ratings do not mean identical strengths, weaknesses, reasoning, or sensitivity to wording.

INTERPRETATION BOUNDARY

A first inspection

Five papers, one evaluator, one replicate, and no human reference labels. The narrow score range and shared paper versions limit inference about general effects.

Collection context

The original ICLR pilot system prompt and all thirteen user templates were frozen for this run. A later change to twelve conditions and venue-specific system prompts is outside this experiment.

Collection progressed from 10 paper workers to 32, then up to 64 concurrent review calls. Queue order was deterministic. Authors and dates remained visible inside the original PDFs.

05 / FROZEN INSTRUCTIONS

Prompts and wording reflection

The exact original instructions used in this pilot are embedded below. Reflection records issues to consider in a future experiment; it does not alter these prompts or claim a new run.



Templates are shown verbatim, including placeholders. During collection, OTHER_MODEL_NAME was Kimi K3 and PAPER_CONTENT referred to the local manuscript. Authorship labels are experimental wording, not verified claims about actual authorship.


Rating anchors may constrain the range
The system asks for critical evaluation, mentions an acceptance rate of about 30%, and tells the evaluator to use both threshold-adjacent scores sparingly. Only scores 1 and 3 occurred. These wording choices could contribute to a compressed rating range, but the observed results do not identify their causal effect or establish that the ratings are wrong.
The baseline was repeated
The quality and neutral templates are byte-identical. Their eighteen paired ratings agree, while their review texts differ. Preserve both condition identifiers in this historical release; merging them would erase the distinction between separate calls and shared instructions.
Attribution and context remain visible
The authorship conditions assert that the assistant, a named model, the user, or a collaborator wrote the manuscript. The PDFs retain their authors and dates, so the effect of the asserted attribution cannot be separated from how the evaluator reconciles it with manuscript evidence. The time-effort conditions vary a stated duration; the sentiment conditions also express a preference about acceptance.
Score equality is not semantic equality
No OA change does not imply absence of framing sensitivity. Strengths and weaknesses can differ in emphasis, detail, or interpretation while mapping to the same coarse ordinal category. This report exposes complete text for inspection; it does not supply human labels, a validated semantic effect estimate, or a causal explanation.
